name: Shendu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: No Shendu-specific description found; closest is Savidge 1908, A Grammar and Dictionary of the Lakher Language (archive.org, read — covers related Mara/Lakher, note: final long vowels 'not as a rule accented'), not Shendu proper
earlier_scan.note: Only closely-related Mara/Lakher documented; Shendu-proper stress undescribed

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page for shen1247 (Shendu) and ISO 639-3 registry page for shl / change request 2025-055 (read online 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Identity only. Glottolog: 'Shendu is but a colonial-time appellation for the Mara Chin' [mrh]; no descriptive references listed (n=0); cites Lewin 1869, Tickell 1852, Hughes 1881 as name sources. ISO 639-3 CR 2025-055 (adopted, effective 2026-07-15): shl retired as a duplicate, replaced by mrh (Mara), 'Shendu' added as a name of mrh.

sources.citation: Löffler, Lorenz G. 2004. Some notes on Maraa: II. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 27(1): 61-87. doi:10.15144/LTBA-27.1.61 (also 10.32655/ltba.27.1.03, hdl 10356/177976)
sources.note: Dialect comparison (Tlongsai vs Sabeu), tones and sandhi contours, prefixes, reconstruction. No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' at all (re-grepped today).

sources.citation: Löffler, Lorenz G. 2002. Some notes on Maraa. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 25(1): 123-136. doi:10.15144/LTBA-25.1.123 (also 10.32655/ltba.25.1.05, hdl 10356/178032)
sources.note: §2 'Phonemes and tones' (pp. 124-127): three tones (low, high, mid); Savidge and Lorrain 'failed to recognize the importance of tones'; Lorrain's few lines on tones (his p. 59) 'mostly wrong'. The only 'stress' mentions are vowel-internal: diphthong /ie/ 'with the stress on the second vowel; a Frenchman would have written it /ié/' (p. 126) and 'MM /ie/ (with the stress on a very narrow [e])' (p. 133). No word-stress statement (re-grepped today).

sources.citation: Lorrain, Reginald Arthur. 1951. Grammar and dictionary of the Lakher or Mara language. Gauhati: Government of Assam, Dept. of Historical and Antiquarian Studies. x+372 pp. — ONLY the 3 Rosetta Project pages (title, introduction, Part I Orthography)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan): WID Old Widener 1286.180 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Orthography only: 'there are only a very few instances where the vowel needs a circumflex accent placed over it to increase the length of that sound... forgetting to accent such a vowel or vice versa changes the meaning entirely' — 'accent' = length diacritic, not stress. Full grammar (pp. 1-59, tone note reported by Löffler at p. 59) not open: HathiTrust record 000756017 is search-only per catalog page returned a block page to automated fetch today); Harvard print WID 1286.180.

sources.citation: Hughes, W. Gwynne. 1881. The hill tracts of Arakan. Rangoon: Government Press. (Glottolog ref 99257; vocabulary of Chin, Shandoo/Pooee and Kamee mostly by Davis 1867-68)
sources.note: Vocabulary appendix (scanned from line 3287, 'Chin / Shandoo or Pooee / Kamee'); preface pp. 47-48 only says the list is Davis's with corrections and additions. No accent/stress/pronunciation note (grep: only 'distress' and 'more stress upon the brighter side').

sources.citation: Lewin, Thomas Herbert. 1869. The hill tracts of Chittagong and the dwellers therein; with comparative vocabularies of the hill dialects. Calcutta: Bengal Secretariat Press. 164 pp. (Glottolog ref 29610)
sources.note: Comparative vocabulary (Mru, Khyeng, Lhoosai, Bunjogi, Pankho, Shendu columns; scanned from line 12550) with no pronunciation or accent notes anywhere in the book (grep accent|stress|emphas: only 'distresses', 'mistresses', 'emphasize' in ethnographic prose). Ethnographic sketch of the 'Shendoos' pp. ~90-92.

sources.citation: Arden, Michelle J. 2010. A phonetic, phonological, and morphosyntactic analysis of the Mara language. MA thesis, San Jose State University (Master's Theses 3744). doi:10.31979/etd.v36r-dk3u. 105 PDF pp. (Glottolog: 179 pp., hhtype grammar, listed under mara1382)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing on word stress, accent or prominence (grep stress|accent|prominen: only 'stress that these early researchers...' p. 14 and 'less prominent' syntactic position). Ch. 5 Phonetic Inventory §5.3 'Three-tone System' (p. 49, PDF p. 60): 'The Mara language is primarily a three-tone system, although some exceptions exist... There is ample evidence that all three tones are contrastive.' §6.3 Tones (pp. 63-66): three level tones + a rare, mostly morphologically induced falling contour tone. Sabeu dialect consultant. Silent on stress. fetched sources via the Wayback Machine (snapshot 20240405133…

sources.citation: Savidge, Fred W. 1908. A grammar and dictionary of the Lakher language. Allahabad: Pioneer Press. 225 pp.
sources.note: 'Lakher alphabet and pronunciation' pp. 1-2 only. Footnote to the circumflexed long vowels: '* The final vowels of words and syllables being generally long, they are not as a rule accented.' — 'accented' = carrying the circumflex length mark (orthography), not word stress. No stress description; tones not recognised.

sources.citation: Tickell, S. R. 1852. Notes on the Heumá or "Shendoos," a tribe inhabiting the hills north of Arracan. Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal 21: 207-243. (Glottolog ref 303875, wordlist, 'Shendoos = Shendu = Mara Chin [mrh]')
sources.note: Only Shendu-proper primary source. Vocabulary preface (pp. 212-213) says just 'The dialect is exceedingly guttural, gh being exactly rendered by the Arabic [ghain] and kh by the Persian [khe] while in their vowel sounds éw and ü have precisely the sounds of the French vowels in deux, and u in flute'. Nothing on accent, stress or tone (grep accent|pronunc|tone|syllab over the paper: no hits). Wordlist + sentences follow.
